question: An 85-year-old man with terminal stage colon cancer formally designates his best friend as his medical durable power of attorney. After several courses of chemotherapy and surgical intervention, the patient’s condition does not improve, and he soon develops respiratory failure. He is then placed on a ventilator in a comatose condition. His friend with the medical power of attorney tells the care provider that the patient would not want to be on life support. The patient’s daughter disputes this and says that her father needs to keep receiving care, in case there should be any possibility of recovery. Additionally, there is a copy of the patient’s living will in the medical record which states that, if necessary, he should be placed on life support until full recovery. Which of the following is the most appropriate course of action?

options.opa: The durable medical power of attorney’s decision should be followed.
options.opb: Follow the daughter’s decision for the patient
options.opc: Contact other family members to get their input for the patient
options.opd: Act according to the patient’s living will
options.ope: Withdraw the life support since the patient’s chances of recovery are very low

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Patient designates best friend as medical durable power of attorney -> Friend states patient would not want to be on life support -> Daughter disputes friend's decision -> Daughter believes patient should keep receiving care for any possibility of recovery -> Copy of patient's living will in medical record states to be placed on life support until full recovery -> Act according to the patient's living will -> 95%
analysis: In this scenario, the patient has designated his best friend as his medical durable power of attorney, who has communicated the patient's wishes to not be on life support. Additionally, the patient's living will also states that he should be placed on life support until full recovery if necessary. Given the legal authority of the medical durable power of attorney and the patient's documented wishes in the living will, the most appropriate course of action would be to follow the patient's living will.
